title: IRF1-mediated thioredoxin (TXN) protects multiple myeloma cells from ferroptosis through remodeling of PUFA-containing phospholipids
task: Identify ferroptosis resistance mechanisms in multiple myeloma
key_results: TXN knockdown enhanced ferroptosis and lipid peroxidation; IRF1-TXN axis regulates PUFA-phospholipid remodeling; TXN targeting restored bortezomib sensitivity
comments: Study elegantly connects redox biology to phospholipid remodeling in ferroptosis, with clear therapeutic implications for overcoming drug resistance.

model_io.model: Multiple myeloma cell lines with genetic/pharmacological TXN modulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: TXN suppresses ferroptosis by remodeling PUFA-containing phospholipids
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TXN inhibition induced PUFA-PL remodeling and increased ferroptosis susceptibility

hypotheses.hypothesis: IRF1 acts as transcriptional repressor of TXN in MM
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: IRF1 depletion increased TXN expression and reduced ferroptosis

hypotheses.hypothesis: TXN inhibition restores ferroptotic vulnerability in BTZ-resistant MM
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TXN targeting enhanced BTZ sensitivity

title: Administration of a phosphodiesterase 4B inhibitor reduces hippocampal neuronal cell death after global cerebral ischemia
task: Reduce hippocampal neuronal death after global cerebral ischemia
key_results: AMX treatment reduced neuronal degeneration and preserved neuronal integrity; increased lysosomal and autophagic protein markers

model_io.model: Mouse global cerebral ischemia model with post-ischemia treatment

hypotheses.hypothesis: PDE4B inhibition reduces ischemia-induced neuronal death via lysosome/autophagy modulation

title: Salidroside ameliorates glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis by regulating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway: a network pharmacology and in vivo
task: Evaluate salidroside protection against glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis via PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway
key_results: Salidroside increased bone mineral density (p<0.001) and osteoblast markers (OC, ALP); upregulated PI3K/Akt/mTOR mRNA and protein expression; reduced oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines (p<0.001)
comments: Network pharmacology predictions validated in vivo, but the precise mechanisms linking pathway activation to bone cell differentiation remain incompletely characterized.

Network pharmacology and molecular docking

hypotheses.hypothesis: Salidroside activates PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to promote osteoblast function and bone formation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Salidroside increased BMD and osteoblast markers; enhanced pathway protein expression

hypotheses.hypothesis: Salidroside reduces oxidative stress and inflammation to protect bone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Significant reduction in oxidative stress and inflammatory cytokines

title: Unexpected functional role of the transactivation domain for nuclear import of STAT5
task: Characterize role of transactivation domain (TAD) in STAT5 nuclear import
key_results: TAD-deficient STAT5 mutants retained in cytoplasm; 12-amino-acid TAD stretch restored nuclear translocation; residues D754 and D758 essential for nuclear import; single intact TAD in dimer sufficient for import
comments: Unexpected finding that TAD has distinct function in STAT5 versus other STATs, providing mechanistic insights but requiring further structural characterization.

model_io.model: Live-cell imaging of fluorescent STAT5 mutants in STAT5-/- HeLa EpoR cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: STAT5 transactivation domain is required for cytokine-stimulated nuclear import
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TAD-deficient STAT5 showed impaired nuclear translocation after Epo stimulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: D754 and D758 residues in TAD are critical for nuclear import function
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Mutation of these residues prevented nuclear translocation of phosphorylated STAT5

hypotheses.hypothesis: TAD function in STAT5 nuclear trafficking differs from other STAT family members
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: TAD has unique role distinct from canonical transcriptional activation function

title: SpaCEy links spatial tissue patterns to clinical outcomes using explainable graph neural networks

title: Early insights into predicted efficacy of Ebola monoclonal antibodies for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
task: Assessing monoclonal antibody efficacy against Bundibugyo virus using structural modeling
key_results: mAb114 (Ebanga) binding compromised by E112D/P116A mutations; MBP134 cocktail epitopes conserved; Inmazeb shows complex synergistic binding despite individual component failures
comments: Urgent computational work addressing active outbreak, but predictions require experimental neutralization validation and structural models are computational proxies.

model_io.model: Structural modeling and epitope conservation analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: BDBV outbreak isolates carry mutations disrupting mAb114 but not MBP134 epitopes
hypotheses.result: E112D/P116A mutations in mAb114 binding site identified; MBP134 epitopes conserved across 44 sequences

hypotheses.hypothesis: Inmazeb cocktail components exhibit synergistic trimeric binding despite individual component failures
hypotheses.result: Structural modeling predicted BDBV synergistic binding for complete trimer but not individual mAbs

title: Left-right asymmetry in the breast TME is associated with distinct bioelectric and epigenetic tumor features

key_results: Right-sided tumors display higher stromal/CAF signatures; left-sided tumors show depolarized membrane potential; GJA1 hypermethylation links methylation and bioelectricity

title: Local versus central differential privacy under final-model privacy attacks in low-client-count cross-silo federated learning

comments: Separates training-time from final-model confidentiality; practical finding: mechanism choice depends on attacker model and privacy unit, not label alone.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Record-level DP-SGD outperforms client-level mechanisms via privacy amplification by subsampling

title: Emergent charge crystallization and frustration in a particle anti-spin ice

model_io.model: Colloidal particles with fast-rotating in-plane magnetic field on bipartite (square, honeycomb) and non-bipartite (pentaheptite) lattices

hypotheses.hypothesis: Inverted interaction paradigm (attraction vs. repulsion) produces anti-spin ice maximizing rather than minimizing charges
hypotheses.result: Confirmed experimentally and via simulation across multiple lattice geometries

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pentaheptite lattice connectivity with unequal polygon sides creates topological charge frustration
hypotheses.result: Demonstrated suppression of charge crystallization at high interaction strengths
